newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Leumi heads for Europe roadshow.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Leumi heads for Europe roadshow.

text.p: The heads of Israel's Bank Leumi and MI Holdings, the agency charged with selling state-owned banks, were scheduled to leave for a European roadshow on Sunday to woo investors for a share offering.
"We will offer between 10 and 15 percent of Leumi and we expect foreign institutional investors will purchase some 70 to 75 percent," said Meir Jacobsen, MI Holdings managing director.
The government holds 82 percent of Leumi, Israel's second largest bank.
Jacobsen said the government hoped to raise about 500 million shekels ($150 million) from the sale, which is due to take place later in May.

The bank chiefs were due to meet investors in Switzerland, England and Scotland. Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers are the international distributors for the offering which will include shares and warrants.
The government expects to raise three billion shekels from the sale of Israeli bank shares this year.

Separately, the central bank's supervisor of banks asked two groups of investors bidding for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim to reduce their debt to the bank as a condition of purchase, the Haaretz newspaper said on Sunday.
The first group, known as the Keil-Fishman group, is led by U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil, while the other is led by U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison of Carnival Cruise Lines.
The central bank declined comment on the report.
The debt of each of the two groups is equal to more than 10 percent of Hapoalim's equity capital, Haaretz said.
The government owns 78 percent of Hapoalim, Israel's largest commercial bank. It aims to sell between 25 and 69.3 percent of its stake through the tender which it hopes to complete by mid-August.
